name: Do I need permits for a primary suite addition in San Diego, Chula Vista, or Coronado?

mainEntity.name: Do I need permits for a primary suite addition in San Diego, Chula Vista, or Coronado?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Do not begin construction until the required plans, approvals, and permits are confirmed for the property’s jurisdiction. Adding square footage or changing plumbing, electrical, structural, or mechanical systems can require review; San Diego’s official guidance says permits are required before constructing or expanding a single-family home and for listed building-system work.

Requirements differ among San Diego, Chula Vista, Coronado, National City, Imperial Beach, and other jurisdictions, and an HOA or coastal-area condition may add another review layer. A contractor should verify the applicable authority rather than assume a neighboring city’s process applies.

Key factors:
- Exact city or unincorporated jurisdiction
- Setbacks, lot coverage, and easements
- Structural, energy, plumbing, electrical, and mechanical scope
- HOA or design-review requirements where applicable

Practical guidance: Ask for a permit responsibility matrix and a copy of the approved plan set before demolition or construction. Treat permit fees and review time as separate budget and schedule items.

Elite Remodeling & Design identifies permitting and construction coordination as parts of its residential addition process.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually, an addition that expands the home or changes structural, plumbing, electrical, or mechanical systems requires jurisdiction-specific review. San Diego requires permits before constructing or expanding a single-family home. Confirm the exact property jurisdiction, HOA requirements, and permit scope before work begins.
